Eric Williams was the historian who led Trinidad and Tobago to independence on 31 August 1962 and governed it as prime minister until his death in 1981.

His book Capitalism and Slavery (1944) argued that Britain ended slavery because it no longer paid, not only from moral feeling. The thesis is still debated and made him famous across the Caribbean.

In 1956 he founded the People's National Movement and won power after lectures in Woodford Square, which he called the University of Woodford Square. He backed the West Indies Federation, used oil money for schools and state firms, and faced the Black Power Revolution of 1970. Trinidad became a republic in 1976 while he led it.
sum: Eric Williams was the historian who led Trinidad and Tobago to independence on 31 August 1962 and governed it as prime minister until his death in 1981.
